finding.claim: OS command injection: the unauthenticated /ping endpoint concatenates the user-supplied `host` query parameter into a shell command string passed to exec(), so shell metacharacters execute arbitrary commands.
finding.source: HTTP GET /ping query parameter `host` (req.query.host), attacker-controlled, no authentication
finding.sink: child_process.exec("ping -c 1 " + req.query.host) at tools.js:7, which runs via a shell; output is returned in the response at line 11

trace.note: Route handler for GET /ping receives the unauthenticated request
req.query.host is concatenated into the command string and passed to exec(), which spawns /bin/sh -c
Command stdout is sent back to the attacker, giving direct output of injected commands. The payload `host=8.8.8.8;id` or `$(id)` also works.

finding.guards_checked: No input validation or allowlist on host, no authentication or authorization middleware, no use of execFile or an argument array, and no escaping. Also no rate limiting. The app.listen(3001) call binds all interfaces. /version uses execFile with a fixed argument array and /uptime runs a constant command, so neither is injectable.

verdict.reason: tools.js:7 passes "ping -c 1 " + req.query.host to shell-spawning exec() with no auth middleware, validation, or escaping anywhere in the file, and tools.js:11 returns stdout (a payload like `8.8.8.8;id` exits 0, so output is returned).

verdict_facts.reason: tools.js:7 passes "ping -c 1 " + req.query.host to exec() (shell) with no auth middleware, validation or escaping in the only file (tools.js:4-28), and tools.js:11 returns stdout, so `host=8.8.8.8;id` gives anonymous command execution.
